category: Generative AI II (2024-2026 features), Photoshop cloud API endpoints and the plugin ecosystem
description: Features added in Photoshop 26.x-27.x that the first generative-AI category predates (Harmonize, Generative Upscale, partner models, Rotate Object, reflection removal, AI Assisted Editor, Selection and Adjustment Brush tools, the new adjustment layers), the individual REST endpoints of the Photoshop API in Adobe Firefly Services, and the plugin distribution/legacy surfaces (CEP, Generator, Exchange, Plugins panel).

tools.name: Harmonize
tools.description: Firefly-powered compositing (Photoshop 27.0, October 2025): select a placed object layer and Harmonize removes its background, then matches its lighting direction, colour temperature, shadows and reflections to the background plate so the composite looks photographed in place. Output goes to a new layer with variations, leaving the original untouched; each generation consumes generative credits (5 per generation at launch).
tools.usage: Select the object layer > Contextual Task Bar > Harmonize (or Edit > Harmonize) > Generate > pick a variation in Properties

parameters.name: Source layer
parameters.description: The cut-out (or uncut) object; background is removed automatically.

parameters.name: Variations
parameters.description: Three results; regenerate for more.

parameters.name: Output
parameters.description: New layer above the source; the source can be hidden.

tools.example: Place a product shot on a lifestyle background, scale it, click Harmonize in the task bar; choose the variation whose shadow matches the scene light, then mask minor edge issues.
tools.notes: Requires sign-in and credits; results are labelled with Content Credentials. Works best when the object is roughly correctly sized and placed first.

tools.name: Generative Upscale
tools.description: AI enlargement (Photoshop 27.0) with a choice of models - Adobe's Firefly upscaler (up to 6144 x 6144 px, 37.7 MP) and Topaz Labs' Gigapixel models (Standard, High Fidelity, Recover, Redefine...) licensed inside Photoshop - producing sharp detail where Image Size interpolation would blur. Also exposed to UXP as `Document.generativeUpscale()` (27.2). Use it for low-resolution assets, crops and old scans before print.
tools.usage: Image > Generative Upscale... (also Contextual Task Bar) > choose model > scale (2x/4x or target size) > Generate

parameters.name: Model
parameters.description: Firefly Upscaler or Topaz Gigapixel model variants.

parameters.name: Scale / Target size
parameters.description: Multiplier or explicit dimensions within the model's limit.

parameters.name: Output
parameters.description: New document or replaces the current layer stack depending on version.

tools.example: Open an 800 px web image, Image > Generative Upscale, Topaz 'High Fidelity' 4x, Generate; compare with Image Size > Preserve Details 2.0 at 100 % zoom.
tools.notes: Consumes generative credits (Topaz models cost more). Camera Raw Super Resolution remains the raw-file route; Neural Filter Super Zoom is the older option.

tools.name: Partner models in Generative Fill and Generate Image (Gemini, FLUX, Firefly Image 4/5)
tools.description: Since Photoshop 27.0 the model picker in Generative Fill offers third-party models alongside Firefly: Google Gemini 2.5 Flash Image ('Nano Banana') and Black Forest Labs FLUX.1 Kontext Pro at launch, FLUX.2 Pro from 27.2 (December 2025), Firefly Image 5 for fills from 27.6 (April 2026), and the same choice arrived in Generate Image in 27.8 (July 2026). Partner models trade Adobe's commercially-safe training for different styles and stronger text/scene understanding; the default 'Firefly Fill & Expand' model (27.3) renders up to 2K linear resolution.
tools.usage: Generative Fill / Generate Image > model picker (dropdown next to the prompt) > Firefly Image 5 / Firefly Fill & Expand / Gemini 2.5 Flash Image / FLUX.1 Kontext Pro / FLUX.2 Pro > prompt > Generate

parameters.name: Model
parameters.description: Adobe Firefly models (commercially safe, Content Credentials) or partner models (may not be indemnified; check licensing).

parameters.name: Prompt / Reference
parameters.description: Text prompt; reference image (Firefly) or reference objects (27.3+).

parameters.name: Credits
parameters.description: Partner models consume more credits per generation; balance shown in the task bar (27.6+).

tools.example: Select an empty tabletop, Generative Fill, model FLUX.2 Pro, prompt 'ceramic espresso cup with saucer, soft window light', Generate, then compare with Firefly Image 5 for a cleaner integration.
tools.notes: Partner models are cloud-hosted by the partner; some regions/enterprise accounts disable them. Enterprise admins can restrict models in the Admin Console.

tools.name: Reference objects (Generative Fill)
tools.description: Added in 27.3 (January 2026): instead of a whole reference image, you can point Generative Fill at a specific object - a layer, a selection or an uploaded cut-out - and the model inserts that object (same product, logo, garment) into the selected area with matching perspective and lighting. Use it for product placement and brand-consistent variations.
tools.usage: Make a selection > Generative Fill > Reference icon > choose Object > pick a layer or upload > optional prompt > Generate

parameters.name: Reference type
parameters.description: Image (style/composition) or Object (insert this thing).

parameters.name: Source
parameters.description: Open document layer, file, or Libraries asset.

tools.example: Select the shelf area, Generative Fill > Reference > Object > choose the 'bottle' layer, prompt 'placed on the shelf, front label visible', Generate.
tools.notes: Object fidelity is best with clean cut-outs; small text on labels may still be regenerated. Firefly models only at launch.

tools.name: Rotate Object
tools.description: Photoshop 27.6 (April 2026): rotates a flat 2D cut-out in 3D space with an on-canvas widget and live preview - the model synthesises the unseen sides and re-lights the object - then renders the final result at full resolution as a new layer. Useful for turning a product shot a few degrees to match a scene, or for showing an alternative angle without a reshoot.
tools.usage: Select the object layer > Contextual Task Bar / Edit > Rotate Object > drag the 3D handles (yaw/pitch) > Generate

parameters.name: Rotation widget
parameters.description: Drag to set yaw and pitch; preview updates in real time.

parameters.name: Generate
parameters.description: Renders at full resolution using generative credits.

tools.example: Cut out a sneaker with Remove Background, Rotate Object, drag 30 degrees left, Generate, then Harmonize it onto the new background.
tools.notes: Large rotations invent detail and may alter logos; keep within roughly 45 degrees for fidelity.

tools.name: Distraction Removal (Find Distractions: Wires and Cables, People, Reflections)
tools.description: The Remove tool's automatic modes: Find Distractions detects and removes power lines and cables (26.0), background people (26.0) and, from 27.6, window reflections in one click, with the tool's Generative AI mode (Auto / On / Off) deciding whether Firefly or on-device content-aware fill is used. 27.6 also added the 'Find Distractions' entry in the Contextual Task Bar and improved detection accuracy.
tools.usage: Remove tool (J) > options bar > Find Distractions > Wires and Cables / People / Reflections   |   Mode: Auto / Generative AI On / Off

parameters.name: Find Distractions
parameters.description: Detector to run; results show as a preview overlay before applying.

parameters.name: Mode
parameters.description: Auto (may use generative AI), Generative AI On (cloud, credits), Off (on-device).

parameters.name: Remove after each stroke
parameters.description: Apply immediately vs accumulate strokes.

tools.example: Open a street photo, Remove tool > Find Distractions > People; review the highlighted bystanders, click Apply, then brush over the remaining wires with Remove after each stroke on.
tools.notes: On-device mode is free and offline. The same detectors power Camera Raw's Distraction Removal (ACR 17/18).

tools.name: AI Assisted Editor (prompt-based editing)
tools.description: Photoshop 27.10 (August 2026) introduced a conversational editor: type instructions such as 'brighten the shadows, remove the person on the left and make the sky warmer' and the assistant plans and applies the corresponding Photoshop operations (adjustment layers, Remove, Generative Fill, masks) as editable layers, explaining each step. It complements rather than replaces the panels, and every action remains undoable and inspectable in the Layers panel.
tools.usage: Window > AI Assisted Editor (or the assistant icon in the Contextual Task Bar) > type a prompt > review the proposed steps > Apply

parameters.name: Prompt
parameters.description: Natural-language editing request; can reference selections and layers.

parameters.name: Plan review
parameters.description: Steps are listed before application; individual steps can be skipped.

parameters.name: Output
parameters.description: Non-destructive layers/masks where possible; generative steps consume credits.

tools.example: Select the subject, open the AI Assisted Editor, type 'soften skin slightly, add a subtle vignette and match the colour temperature to daylight', Apply, then tweak the generated adjustment layers.
tools.notes: Requires internet and sign-in; availability rolled out by region and plan. Automation pipelines should still use actions/scripts - the assistant is interactive.

tools.name: Generative Workspace
tools.description: A dedicated ideation space (Photoshop 26.0 beta, October 2024; later releases) for generating many image and variation candidates in a grid from prompts, references, style presets and models without touching the working document; favourites can be sent into the document as layers, and prompts/settings are kept per session. Think of it as Firefly's Text-to-Image board embedded in Photoshop.
tools.usage: Window > Generative Workspace (or Contextual Task Bar > Generate Image > Open Generative Workspace) > prompt / settings > Generate > drag a result into the document

parameters.name: Prompt / Model / Style / Aspect ratio
parameters.description: Generation settings including partner models (27.8+).

parameters.name: Reference image
parameters.description: Guide composition or style.

parameters.name: Add to document / Download
parameters.description: Send a result to the canvas as a new layer or save it.

tools.example: Open the Generative Workspace, prompt 'minimalist product backdrop, warm beige, soft shadows', generate 4 variants at 16:9, drag the best into the PSD and place the product on top.
tools.notes: Was a Technology Preview in 26.x; generation consumes credits. Results carry Content Credentials.

tools.name: Selection Brush Tool
tools.description: Photoshop 26.0 tool (nested with the Lasso tools, L / Shift+L) that paints a selection directly with a brush, showing it as a colour overlay like Quick Mask but with add/subtract modes in the options bar, brush size/hardness and the usual Select and Mask hand-off. Faster than Quick Mask for hand-painted selections and more intuitive than the Quick Selection tool on flat colour.
tools.usage: Toolbar > Lasso group > Selection Brush Tool (Shift+L to cycle) > options bar: Add / Subtract, Size, Hardness, Overlay colour/opacity

parameters.name: Mode
parameters.description: Add (default) or Subtract; Alt toggles.

parameters.name: Size / Hardness
parameters.description: Brush settings ([ ] keys).

parameters.name: Overlay
parameters.description: Colour and opacity of the selection overlay; Show Overlay toggle.

tools.example: Press L, Shift+L to the Selection Brush, paint over the sky with a large soft brush, Alt-paint to remove the roof, then click Select and Mask to refine.
tools.notes: The overlay is visual only - the result is a normal selection. Pressure sensitivity works with a tablet.

tools.name: Adjustment Brush Tool
tools.description: Photoshop 26.0 tool (nested with the Brush tools, B / Shift+B) that paints an adjustment onto part of the image: choose the adjustment type (Brightness/Contrast, Levels, Curves, Exposure, Vibrance, Hue/Saturation, Color Balance, Black & White, Photo Filter, Channel Mixer, Color Lookup, Invert, Posterize, Threshold, Gradient Map, Selective Color) in the options bar, paint, and Photoshop creates a masked adjustment layer whose mask is your strokes and whose settings stay editable in Properties.
tools.usage: Toolbar > Brush group > Adjustment Brush Tool (Shift+B) > options bar: Adjustment type, Size, Hardness, Opacity/Flow > paint on canvas

parameters.name: Adjustment
parameters.description: Any adjustment-layer type; one layer per continuous painting session.

parameters.name: Brush settings
parameters.description: Size, hardness, opacity, flow, smoothing; Alt to subtract from the mask.

parameters.name: Properties panel
parameters.description: Edit the adjustment values after painting; the mask remains editable.

tools.example: Select Adjustment Brush, Adjustment = Curves, paint over the face; in Properties raise the curve midpoint for a local dodge; press Alt and paint to trim the mask.
tools.notes: It is a shortcut for 'new adjustment layer + Hide All mask + paint white'; everything remains non-destructive.

tools.name: Color and Vibrance (adjustment layer)
tools.description: A native adjustment layer (Photoshop 27.3.1, early 2026) that brings Camera Raw's colour block to the Layers panel: white balance with Temperature, Tint and a neutral-point eyedropper, plus Vibrance and Saturation, all non-destructive, maskable and blendable. Replaces the round-trip to Camera Raw Filter for simple colour temperature fixes.
tools.usage: Layer > New Adjustment Layer > Color and Vibrance...  (Adjustments panel icon)

parameters.name: Temperature / Tint
parameters.description: -100..100 warm/cool and green/magenta shifts.

parameters.name: White balance eyedropper
parameters.description: Click a neutral to set Temperature/Tint.

parameters.name: Vibrance / Saturation
parameters.description: -100..100 smart and linear saturation.

tools.example: Add Color and Vibrance, click the eyedropper on a grey wall, then Vibrance +25; clip it to the foreground layer with Ctrl+Alt+G.
tools.notes: Distinct from the older Vibrance adjustment layer (which lacks white balance). Not scriptable through the ExtendScript DOM; use Action Manager/batchPlay recorded descriptors.

tools.name: Clarity and Dehaze (adjustment layer)
tools.description: Photoshop 27.3 (January 2026) adjustment layer providing Camera Raw's Clarity (midtone local contrast) and Dehaze (atmospheric haze removal/addition) as live, maskable layer controls with the full range of blend modes and opacity. Use it instead of High Pass/Overlay or the Camera Raw Filter for punch and haze control in composites.
tools.usage: Layer > New Adjustment Layer > Clarity and Dehaze...

parameters.name: Clarity
parameters.description: -100..100 midtone contrast.

parameters.name: Dehaze
parameters.description: -100..100 haze reduction (+) or fog (-).

tools.example: Add Clarity and Dehaze above a landscape, Dehaze +30, Clarity +15, then paint the mask black over the subject's skin.
tools.notes: Heavy Dehaze shifts colour; follow with the Color and Vibrance layer. GPU accelerated.

tools.name: Grain (adjustment layer)
tools.description: Photoshop 27.3 adjustment layer that adds film-style grain non-destructively with Amount, Size and Roughness (the Camera Raw grain model), replacing the old workflow of Add Noise on a 50 % grey Overlay layer or the Filter Gallery Grain effect. Being an adjustment layer it can be masked, blended and re-tuned any time and re-renders correctly after resizing.
tools.usage: Layer > New Adjustment Layer > Grain...

parameters.name: Amount
parameters.description: 0-100 grain strength.

parameters.name: Size
parameters.description: 0-100 grain particle size.

parameters.name: Roughness
parameters.description: 0-100 regularity of the grain.

tools.example: Add Grain (Amount 20, Size 30, Roughness 50) as the top layer of a composite so every element shares the same texture.
tools.notes: Grain is generated at document resolution; downsampling for web changes its appearance, so add it after resizing or at the final size.

tools.name: Light (adjustment layer)
tools.description: Photoshop 27.10 (August 2026) adjustment layer that groups Camera Raw's Light controls - Exposure, Contrast, Highlights, Shadows, Whites, Blacks - into one non-destructive layer, replacing separate Exposure/Levels/Curves/Shadows-Highlights layers for basic tonal work and matching the behaviour photographers know from Lightroom.
tools.usage: Layer > New Adjustment Layer > Light...

parameters.name: Exposure / Contrast
parameters.description: Global brightness (stops) and midtone contrast.

parameters.name: Highlights / Shadows / Whites / Blacks
parameters.description: Range-specific recovery and end-point controls.

tools.example: Add Light, Highlights -40, Shadows +25, Whites +10 for a quick HDR-style balance, masked to the foreground.
tools.notes: Shadows/Highlights (Image > Adjustments) remains the destructive alternative. Available on 8/16-bit RGB documents.

tools.name: Photoshop API v1 endpoints (/pie/psdService/*)
tools.description: The original Photoshop API surface at https://image.adobe.io: POST /pie/psdService/documentCreate (new PSD from layers), /documentOperations (edit layers, text, smart objects, effects), /renditionCreate (render PSD to JPEG/PNG/TIFF/PSD), /smartObject (replace smart object content), /text (edit text layers), /photoshopActions (play .atn), /actionJSON (play inline actionJSON), /productCrop (crop to subject), /depthBlur (Neural Filter depth blur), /artboardCreate, /documentManifest (layer tree JSON) and GET /pie/psdService/status/{jobId}. All are asynchronous: the POST returns a job URL to poll.

parameters.name: inputs[].storage
parameters.description: external (presigned URL), adobe, azure, dropbox.

parameters.name: outputs[].type
parameters.description: image/jpeg, image/png, image/tiff, image/vnd.adobe.photoshop; width/quality/compression options.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: Operation-specific: layers[] edits, actions[], actionJSON[], fonts[], patterns[], brushes[].

tools.example:
curl -X POST https://image.adobe.io/pie/psdService/renditionCreate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "x-api-key: $CLIENT_ID" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"inputs":[{"href":"'$IN'","storage":"external"}],"outputs":[{"href":"'$OUT'","storage":"external","type":"image/png","width":1200}]}'
# then GET the returned _links.self.href until status is succeeded
tools.notes: v1 is being superseded by v2 (2025-2026): text/actions map to /v2/execute-actions, document operations to /v2/create-composite, manifest to /v2/generate-manifest; depthBlur has no v2 equivalent. Files up to 2 GB in v1 (4 GB in v2).

tools.name: Photoshop API /v2/execute-actions
tools.description: The unified automation endpoint of the v2 API: runs a UXP script (modern JavaScript executed inside a cloud Photoshop), a traditional .atn action file, or inline ActionJSON against the input document, with a `type` discriminant selecting the mode and `scriptOutputPattern` (glob) to capture files the script writes. Replaces v1 photoshopActions, actionJSON, text and productCrop, which are now published as reusable action definitions.
tools.usage:
POST https://image.adobe.io/v2/execute-actions
{ "inputs": [{ "href": "...", "storage": "external" }],
  "options": { "actions": [{ "type": "uxp" | "atn" | "actionJSON", "href": "<script or .atn url>" | "actionJSON": [...] }], "fonts": [], "scriptOutputPattern": "*.png" },
  "outputs": [{ "href": "...", "storage": "external", "type": "image/jpeg" }] }

parameters.name: actions[].type
parameters.description: uxp (JavaScript with require('photoshop')), atn (recorded action set), actionJSON (batchPlay-style JSON).

parameters.name: fonts / patterns / brushes
parameters.description: Additional assets referenced by the actions.

parameters.name: scriptOutputPattern
parameters.description: Glob for files produced by the UXP script to return as outputs.

tools.notes: Poll GET /v2/status/{jobId}. Processing limit 15 minutes; 'Hosted' storage lets Adobe return temporary URLs instead of requiring presigned PUTs. Neural Filters are not available in cloud actions.

tools.name: Photoshop API /v2/create-composite, /v2/generate-manifest and /v2/create-artboard
tools.description: v2 document services: /create-composite builds or edits a PSD declaratively with a unified `operation` model (add/edit/delete layers, text with synthetic bold/italic and letter spacing, smart objects including SVG/TIFF and linked content, groups/artboards, drop-shadow effects) and renders outputs with a `cropMode`; /generate-manifest returns the enriched layer tree (artboard geometry with device presets, text metadata incl. fonts/anti-aliasing/warp, smart-object extraction URLs); /create-artboard assembles artboards from an `images[]` array. All accept the same inputs/outputs storage model.
tools.usage: POST https://image.adobe.io/v2/create-composite   |   POST https://image.adobe.io/v2/generate-manifest   |   POST https://image.adobe.io/v2/create-artboard

parameters.name: operations[]
parameters.description: { operation: 'add' | 'edit' | 'delete', layer: { type: 'textLayer' | 'smartObject' | 'layerSection' | 'adjustmentLayer' ..., name, text, bounds, blendOptions, effects } }.

parameters.name: cropMode
parameters.description: Replaces v1 trimToCanvas/trimToLayer booleans.

parameters.name: storage modes
parameters.description: external, adobe, hosted (Adobe temp URLs), embedded (base64 inline, text only).

tools.example:
1. POST /v2/generate-manifest with the template PSD to learn layer names.
2. POST /v2/create-composite with operations: edit textLayer 'Headline' -> 'Spring Sale', edit smartObject 'Hero' -> new image href; outputs JPEG 1200 px.
3. Poll /v2/status/{jobId}; download the rendition.
tools.notes: File limit 4 GB. Manifest types are snake_case in v2 ('text_layer', 'smart_object'). Linked smart objects require the linked file among inputs.

tools.name: Photoshop API /v2/remove-background (and legacy /sensei/cutout, /sensei/mask)
tools.description: Server-side subject isolation: POST /v2/remove-background returns either the cut-out subject on transparency or a grayscale mask (`mode`), with options for trimming, colour decontamination and mask format, replacing the v1 Image Cutout (/sensei/cutout) and Mask (/sensei/mask) endpoints that reached end-of-life on 15 October 2025. The desktop Remove Background Quick Action is the interactive equivalent (on-device from 27.0).
tools.usage:
POST https://image.adobe.io/v2/remove-background
{ "image": { "source": { "url": "<presigned GET>" } }, "mode": "cutout" | "mask", "output": { "mediaType": "image/png" }, "trim": false, "colorDecontamination": 0.5 }

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: cutout (RGBA PNG) or mask (grayscale).

parameters.name: trim
parameters.description: Crop the output to the subject bounds.

parameters.name: colorDecontamination
parameters.description: 0-1 edge colour clean-up strength.

parameters.name: backgroundColor
parameters.description: Optional fill instead of transparency.

tools.example: curl -X POST https://image.adobe.io/v2/remove-background -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "x-api-key: $CLIENT_ID" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"image":{"source":{"url":"'$IN'"}},"mode":"cutout","output":{"mediaType":"image/png"}}'
tools.notes: Synchronous for typical sizes (returns the result URL directly) unlike the job-based PSD endpoints. Accepts JPEG, PNG, WebP and PSD inputs; see the guide for the current pixel and file-size limits.

tools.name: Lightroom API /v2/edit (autoTone, autoStraighten, presets, XMP)
tools.description: Part of the same Firefly Services family: v1 exposed /lrService/autoTone, /autoStraighten, /presets (apply XMP presets) and /xmp (apply raw develop settings) on JPEG/PNG/TIFF/raw inputs; v2 unifies them as POST /v2/edit with an `adjustments` block (Exposure, Contrast, Highlights, Shadows, Whites, Blacks, Clarity, Vibrance, Saturation, Temperature, Tint, Sharpen, Noise Reduction...) and optional preset/XMP references, polled through /v2/status/{jobId}. Use it to batch-develop raw files in the cloud with Camera Raw's engine.
tools.usage:
POST https://image.adobe.io/v2/edit
{ "inputs": [{ "href": "...", "storage": "external" }], "options": { "autoTone": true, "adjustments": { "exposure": 0.3, "vibrance": 15 }, "xmp": "<presigned xmp url>" }, "outputs": [{ "href": "...", "storage": "external", "type": "image/jpeg", "quality": 90 }] }

parameters.name: autoTone / autoStraighten
parameters.description: Camera Raw auto adjustments.

parameters.name: adjustments
parameters.description: Explicit slider values mirroring the Basic/Detail panels.

parameters.name: xmp / preset
parameters.description: Apply a Lightroom preset or develop settings file.

tools.example: Submit 500 raw files with autoTone and a brand preset XMP; outputs as 2048 px sRGB JPEGs to the bucket; poll each job.
tools.notes: Requires the Firefly Services / Lightroom API entitlement. Masks and AI tools (Denoise, Lens Blur) are not exposed.

tools.name: Photoshop API authentication, storage and job polling
tools.description: Every Firefly Services call needs an Adobe IMS OAuth 2.0 server-to-server access token (client credentials from the Adobe Developer Console project with the Firefly Services / Photoshop API added; scopes openid, AdobeID, read_organizations, firefly_api, ff_apis) sent as `Authorization: Bearer` plus `x-api-key: <client id>`; inputs/outputs are presigned URLs on external storage (S3, Azure Blob, GCS, Dropbox) or Adobe-hosted temp storage (v2), and long-running operations return 202 with a `_links.self.href` job URL to poll (states: pending, running, succeeded, failed) until the output is written to the presigned PUT URL.
tools.usage:
POST https://ims-na1.adobelogin.com/ims/token/v3  (client_id, client_secret, grant_type=client_credentials, scope=openid,AdobeID,read_organizations,firefly_api,ff_apis)  ->  access_token (24 h)
GET https://image.adobe.io/v2/status/{jobId}  (or the _links.self.href from the 202 response)

parameters.name: Rate limits
parameters.description: Per-minute request quotas per client; 429 with Retry-After.

parameters.name: Presigned URL lifetime
parameters.description: Must outlive the job (allow 1 h+).

parameters.name: Errors
parameters.description: 400 (bad input), 401/403 (token/entitlement), 415 (unsupported type), 5xx (retry with backoff).

tools.example:
import requests, time
tok = requests.post('https://ims-na1.adobelogin.com/ims/token/v3', data={'client_id': CID, 'client_secret': SEC, 'grant_type': 'client_credentials', 'scope': 'openid,AdobeID,read_organizations,firefly_api,ff_apis'}).json()['access_token']
h = {'Authorization': f'Bearer {tok}', 'x-api-key': CID, 'Content-Type': 'application/json'}
r = requests.post('https://image.adobe.io/pie/psdService/documentManifest', headers=h, json={'inputs': [{'href': IN_URL, 'storage': 'external'}]})
status = r.json()['_links']['self']['href']
while True:
    s = requests.get(status, headers=h).json()
    if s['outputs'][0]['status'] in ('succeeded', 'failed'): break
    time.sleep(2)
print(s)
tools.notes: JWT service accounts were retired in 2024-2025; use OAuth server-to-server. The Photoshop API SDK (@adobe/photoshop-apis for Node, firefly-services Python samples) wraps token refresh and polling.

tools.name: CEP extensions (legacy HTML panels)
tools.description: The Common Extensibility Platform hosted HTML/CSS/JavaScript panels in a Chromium Embedded Framework with a Node.js runtime, talking to Photoshop through CSInterface.js `evalScript()` calls that run ExtendScript. Defined by CSXS/manifest.xml, installed under the CEP extensions folder or as .zxp packages, and enabled via the PlayerDebugMode registry/plist flag during development. Still loads in current Photoshop (Window > Extensions (legacy)) but is deprecated in favour of UXP; no new CEP APIs are added.
tools.usage: Window > Extensions (legacy) > <panel>   |   Dev: HKCU\Software\Adobe\CSXS.11 PlayerDebugMode=1; folder %AppData%\Adobe\CEP\extensions\<id>\ with CSXS/manifest.xml, index.html, jsx/host.jsx   |   var cs = new CSInterface(); cs.evalScript('app.activeDocument.name', function(r){...});

parameters.name: CSXS/manifest.xml
parameters.description: ExtensionBundleId, Extension Id/Version, HostList (PHXS/PHSP with version range), MainPath, ScriptPath, UI type (Panel/Modeless/ModalDialog), sizes, CEFCommandLine parameters.

parameters.name: CSInterface.js
parameters.description: evalScript, getHostEnvironment, addEventListener (CSEvent), openURLInDefaultBrowser, requestOpenExtension.

parameters.name: .zxp packaging
parameters.description: Signed with ZXPSignCmd; installed with ExManCmd / Anastasiy's Extension Manager / Creative Cloud (via Exchange).

tools.example:
1. Set PlayerDebugMode=1 for CSXS.11 (or the CSXS version listed in Help > System Info).
2. Create %AppData%\Adobe\CEP\extensions\com.example.panel\ with CSXS/manifest.xml, index.html (loads CSInterface.js) and jsx/host.jsx.
3. Restart Photoshop, open Window > Extensions (legacy) > Example Panel; debug at http://localhost:<port> from .debug file.
tools.notes: Preferences > Plugins > Load Extension Panels must be on. CEP 11/12 in Photoshop 2024-2026; Apple-silicon builds require CEP 11+. Migrate to UXP for new work (UXP has no Node.js but a sandboxed file API).

tools.name: Generator plugins (Node.js) and Generate Image Assets
tools.description: Generator is a Node.js-based plugin host inside Photoshop (enabled in Preferences > Plugins) that streams document changes to plugins over a socket. Adobe's built-in Image Assets plugin (File > Generate > Image Assets) exports layers automatically when their names carry file extensions and modifiers ('logo.png', '200% logo@2x.png, 50% small.jpg8', 'icon.svg', folder/name.png); third-party generator plugins (generator-core, generator-assets on GitHub) can react to any document event for live previews, design-to-code tools and asset pipelines.
tools.usage: File > Generate > Image Assets (toggle per document)   |   Layer names: 'hero.jpg8' (JPEG quality 80), '32x32 favicon.png', '100% a.png, 200% a@2x.png', 'assets/name.svg'   |   Dev: github.com/adobe-photoshop/generator-core, run `node app.js -f ../plugins` with Generator enabled

parameters.name: Name syntax
parameters.description: [scale% | WxH] name.ext[quality] with commas for multiple outputs; subfolders with '/'.

parameters.name: Default settings layer
parameters.description: A layer named 'default 200% @2x' applies to all assets.

parameters.name: Generator socket
parameters.description: Plugins connect to port 49494 (configurable) via generator-core.

tools.example: Rename layers 'btn.png, 200% btn@2x.png' and 'hero.jpg8', then tick File > Generate > Image Assets: an 'assets' folder next to the PSD updates on every edit.
tools.notes: Requires a saved document. Export As is the manual alternative. Generator is legacy but still shipped; UXP has no equivalent event stream for external processes.

tools.name: Adobe Exchange, Creative Cloud Marketplace and Developer Distribution
tools.description: Distribution channels for Photoshop plugins: users browse and install UXP/CEP plugins (free or paid) from the Creative Cloud Desktop app's Marketplace tab ('Stock & Marketplace > Plugins') or exchange.adobe.com; developers submit .ccx packages, listing metadata, screenshots and pricing through Adobe Developer Distribution (developer.adobe.com/distribute), where Adobe reviews them for API use, security and UX before publication. Enterprise admins can allow-list plugins.
tools.usage: Creative Cloud Desktop > Stock & Marketplace > Plugins > search > Install   |   developer.adobe.com/distribute > Create listing > upload .ccx > submit for review

parameters.name: Listing requirements
parameters.description: Unique manifest id, semver version, icons, description, support URL, privacy policy for network use, review notes.

parameters.name: Private distribution
parameters.description: Unlisted/private listings for enterprise or beta users via invitation links.

tools.example: Package the plugin in UDT, create a Developer Distribution listing, upload exporter_1.0.0.ccx, add screenshots and a test account, submit; after approval users install from the Marketplace and the plugin appears under Plugins in Photoshop.
tools.notes: Updates go through the same review; the Marketplace auto-updates installed plugins. Paid plugins use Adobe's or the developer's own licensing (e.g. Gumroad/Paddle keys checked over the network permission).

tools.name: Plugins menu, Plugins Panel and Manage Plugins
tools.description: The Plugins menu (Photoshop 22+) lists installed UXP plugins with their panels and commands, opens the Plugins Panel (browse/launch installed plugins, links to the Marketplace) and Manage Plugins (opens Creative Cloud Desktop to enable, disable, update or uninstall). Legacy .8bf filters still live under the Filter menu and CEP panels under Window > Extensions (legacy); on Apple-silicon Macs, third-party filter plug-ins that were not rebuilt natively appear only when Photoshop runs under Rosetta.
tools.usage: Plugins > Plugins Panel / Manage Plugins... / <plugin name> > <panel or command>

parameters.name: Plugins Panel
parameters.description: Cards for each installed plugin; click to open panels.

parameters.name: Manage Plugins
parameters.description: Creative Cloud Desktop > Stock & Marketplace > Plugins > Manage plugins: enable/disable, update, uninstall, view permissions.

tools.example: Plugins > Plugins Panel, click 'Alchemist' to open its panel; if a plugin misbehaves, Plugins > Manage Plugins > disable it and restart.
tools.notes: Side-loaded (UDT) plugins appear in the menu with a 'developer' badge and are unloaded when Photoshop restarts unless re-loaded from UDT. Installed plugins live in %AppData%\Adobe\UXP\PluginsStorage\PHSP\<version>\.
